requirement: Supervise background subprocesses, managing lifecycle through termination, signal escalation, exit status reaping, and context manager cleanup.
skeleton: ManagedProcess class with start, is_running, wait, terminate, stop methods and context manager.
caption: A standard-library supervisor for one background child process that always reaps what it starts, with no third-party imports. ManagedProcess takes cmd and an optional environment, raising ValueError unless cmd is a non-empty list of strings. start raises RuntimeError when a previous child is still running and otherwise launches the command through subprocess.Popen with piped stdout and stderr in text mode. is_running returns False before start and otherwise calls poll, which both refreshes and reaps the exit status, returning True only while poll reports no exit code. wait raises RuntimeError before start and otherwise waits with the optional timeout. stop(timeout=1.0) raises RuntimeError before start and ValueError unless the timeout is positive; if the child has already exited it returns the recorded return code, otherwise it sends terminate, waits up to the timeout, and escalates to kill followed by another wait when the child ignores the signal, and in a finally block closes both output pipes. terminate(grace_period=1.0) delegates to stop. The class is a context manager: __enter__ starts the child and __exit__ stops it when it is still running, even after an exception inside the block. The fixture asserts that a normal stop leaves a return code and a non-running child, that a child ignoring the terminate signal after printing READY is killed and reaped, that the context manager cleans up on an exception, that is_running reaps a finished child with code 0, that pipes are closed after stop, and the timeout and command validation.

rationale.teaches: Supervising a child process: poll for liveness, wait with a kill escalation on timeout, terminate only a running process, validate the command vector, and reap on context exit.
rationale.why: A process that is never waited for stays a zombie and returncode stays None, but nothing raises. The fixture checks returncode and whether the pid still exists after stop.

candidates.why_wrong: wait returns 0 without waiting, so the child keeps running and is never reaped.
is_running reads returncode without polling, so a child that already exited is still reported as running.
terminate only acts when the process is not running, so a live process is never signalled.
A timeout of exactly 0 is accepted and every wait expires immediately.
A bare string command is accepted, so Popen receives it as a single program name with no arguments.
